notes.title: Beef Cat Ultra 2.0 Anniversary Update
notes.content: [h1]Happy 1-Year Anniversary to Beef Cat Ultra![/h1][p][/p][p]Beef Cat Ultra released last year on September 23rd 2024. And it has been an excellent year. Out of the gate Beef Cat Ultra reached a smaller audience than we anticipated - such is game development. But we did a handful of polish patches and released the large Remix update for Steam users adding endless endgame content for diehard players.[/p][p]In late December I cold-emailed an indie game publisher and said "hey I think you should publish my game for consoles" but in a slightly more professional way. And when I woke up the next morning I was surprised to see a return email from them saying "we agree, let's talk" exactly as casually as that. A few short months later, Beef Cat Ultra released for the Nintendo Switch consoles, Playstation 4/5, and Xbox One and Series consoles.[/p][p]In the months since, we've been quiet on Beef Cat Ultra while we worked on other projects and tried some new things out. But I've been logging every bit of feedback for the game across all platforms and finished a gargantuan Anniversary Patch late last week. This was a holistic look at every thing in the game. Stage design, assets, code - anything that could be looked at was looked at. And a LOT was tweaked.[/p][p]Let's get into some monster patch notes:[/p][h2]Beef Cat Ultra v2.0 Patch Notes[/h2][h3]Early Game Balancing and Onboarding[/h3][list][*][p]Beef Cat Survives: Removed a chest from near the starting point, replaced some trees with grassy fenced areas.[/p][/*][*][p]Gauntlet Legacy: Moved the first gate closer to the start of the stage so that is shares a screen with the first key, moved a couple early stage enemy spawners, added a bridge over the large body of water to give players another path in a congested space.[/p][/*][*][p]Collectathon: Added extra gemmies to the stage, only requires about 90% of gems for stage clear.[/p][/*][*][p]Funky Lake Stages: visual improvements to create more landmark type spaces in the environment to help with understanding the layout better.[/p][/*][*][p]Broken Forest: changed player starting location, added gemmies, only requires about 90% of gems for stage clear, added an additional path to prevent players getting trapped in the late stage congestion.[/p][/*][/list][h3]General Balancing[/h3][list][*][p]Beef Cat base HP 10 -> 12[/p][/*][*][p]iFrames 10 -> 12[/p][/*][*][p]Froggie base HP 15 -> 18[/p][/*][*][p]Badish HP 10 -> 7[/p][/*][*][p]Fox HP 6 -> 4[/p][/*][*][p]Artibloke HP 20 -> 14[/p][/*][*][p]Big Boss Badish HP 500 -> 400[/p][/*][*][p]Friend Monster HP 650 -> 450[/p][/*][*][p]Added new pickups to all 3 main Metal Mountain stages[/p][/*][*][p]All shops base cost adjusted and cost curve reduced[/p][/*][/list][h3]Visual Changes[/h3][list][*][p]A new title screen![/p][/*][*][p]World Map has less tile bloat which makes the room instance less of a load on the engine[/p][/*][*][p]Tile tweaks to every single stage to increase visual variety[/p][/*][*][p]World region text pop up text smaller and color change, added drop shadow, to improve legibility[/p][/*][/list][h3]Quality of Life Changes[/h3][list][*][p]Added a kill counter to Survive stages that had Steam Achievements tied to a specific kill count[/p][/*][*][p]Pressing Tab (Select on a controller) while in a stage opens audio settings[/p][/*][*][p]Trap signs now spawn world appropriate enemies[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Itemizing out the little changes to every single stage would make this a sprawling changelog that I do not want to type. So, please enjoy that being reduced to "tweaks to every single stage" for my sanity.[/p][p][/p][p]As long as new players are finding Beef Cat Ultra, I'll keep tweaking and improving it. Even as we prepare to launch the Steam page for our next project (the page is currently under review and I was hoping it would be live in time for this update but oh well). If you've played the game, leave a review - it helps us! If you enjoyed it, share it with a friend. Help us make more games by supporting us! We appreciate everyone a ton - whether you hopped in totally in the dark or are a good friend who picked up a copy.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you,[/p][p]Kyle[/p]

notes.title: Beef Cat Ultra Releases on Consoles Worldwide February 7th!
notes.content:
[h1]BLAMMO[/h1]

Happy Monday Beeflandians,

Dropping in to give a long awaited updated on the console version of Beef Cat Ultra! So let's get the big thing out of the way first:

[h2]Beef Cat Ultra Console Version launches Friday, February 7th![/h2]

Developed in partnership with Brainium Games, Beef Cat Ultra will land on Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, Xbox Series S/X, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 worldwide. Localized in SEVEN different languages! Thanks to our publisher for that one. The console version will have full language localization in seven languages: English, German, Spanish (Spain), French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil). A simple toggle in the settings menu lets you change the language on the fly.

There are other differences between the Steam version and the Console version - a font change to help accommodate the localization, full rumble effects across the game, full colorblind accessibility integration across the whole game. The Remix Update, launched last month on Steam, will remain exclusive to the Steam version of the game. Local PvP will also remain exclusive to the Steam version, but the "vs AI" versions of Deathmatch and Volleyball are still in the console version.

Xbox and PlayStation each get a respective set of achievements to hunt. The game is available to pre-order now on Xbox:

[url=https://www.xbox.com/en-us/games/store/beef-cat-ultra/9p6mmzz03qb7]Xbox Store[/url]

The game is available to wishlist on the PlayStation store:

[url=https://store.playstation.com/en-us/concept/10013234]PlayStation Store[/url]

The game is available to wishlist on Nintendo's store and the eShop:

[url=https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/beef-cat-ultra-switch/?srsltid=AfmBOoq5wIhZMs4Vh9w-Hjk1YXdPIgMprJkzjFrvitoIntBZCOcdWmPK]Nintendo Store[/url]

And lastly, you can learn more about our publisher, who did an excellent job handling our console port on their website:

[url=https://www.brainiumgames.com/]Brainium Games[/url]



Thanks for supporting us at Beef Cat and helping us make this a reality! This is such a massive moment for us! It's been my dream since I was just a lil tyke to release a videogame on a Nintendo console, and bam - it's here.

See you Friday!
Kyle

notes.title: v1.1 The Remix Update
notes.content:
[h1]The Remix Update Has Landed[/h1]

[b]Howdy Beeflandians,[/b]

This is a major update that touches every corner of Beef Cat Ultra, adding loads of new content and improving the content that was already there. The Remix Update will kick off a series of much smaller follow-up updates adding new upgrades and items over time to keep the RNG gods of Remix Island pleased. Let's kick off with the main event:

[h2]Added Remix Island[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added Dock and Ship to Stinky Coast
[*] Added Blockerboy to Stinky Coast to lock Remix Island until Game Completion
[*] Added 4 new stages with new mode "Remix"
[*] --Randomized starting location, pickup locations, and enemy spawn locations
[*] --Objective to Kill 5,000 enemies
[*] --Difficulty Tier increases every 5 minutes, increasing enemy health and speed
[*] Added 7 new level up options in Remix mode
[*] --4 New Weapon Level Up Options
[*] --2 New Survival Level Up Options
[*] --1 New Bonus Level Up Options
[*] Added 4 new pickups in Remix mode loot pools
[*] New Shop: Great Reset - Resets all stat purchases at shops to ZERO and does not refund their costs
[*] New Shop: Remix Difficulty - Increases the base Difficulty Tier of Remix Mode by 1
[*] New Weapon: Uppercut - a vertical attack that deals high damage, upgrades increase range
[*] New Weapon: Gross Grass - builds in the environment, has a %chance to spawn a tick, upgrades increase tick spawn chance
[*] New Weapon: Bomb Flower - builds in the environment, trigger to set off an explosion, upgrades reduce planting cooldown
[*] New Passive: Parry Pants - a successful dodge drops a grenade at your feet, upgrades drop more grenades
[/list]

Above is very nearly everything new in Beef Cat Ultra as of today. No bug fixes or tweaks in that section, just new things to challenge yourself on. But that doesn't mean we didn't get around to some great tweaks and fixes.

[h2]Game-Wide Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Optimized Enemy, Object, and Pickup Parent codes - reducing code by 1000+ lines, should improve engine load in late-late endless stages
[*] Bullet based weapons now factor in Damage Modification
[*] Bullet based weapons now factor in Critical Hit Chance
[*] Replaced the font in Shop menus
[*] Added a description tip to every shop
[*] Shop menus no longer display on top of settings menu
[*] Shops can no longer be interacted with while settings menu is open
[*] Re-located player spawn location in "High Seas"
[*] Volleyball pickups now correctly draw a line to Choice Signs
[*] Added subtle controller rumble to enemy kills
[*] Difficulty Tier +1 now gives enemies a single extra HP in Endless stages (at the 10 minute mark)
[*] Added Difficulty Tiers +6-8 to Endless Stages for particularly long games and broken builds
[*] Added new Stat to Stats Screen: Explosion Mod, increase in value increases radius of explosions
[*] New Passive Pickup: Cookbook - increases Explosion Mod by 5
[*] Added Cookbook to World 3/4 Loot Pools and Encyclopedia
[*] Reduced Corpse Bomb explosion radius from 20 -> 16
[*] -Reduced Corpse Bomb frag count from 12 -> 10
[*] -Corpse Bomb, Boom Sticks, and Grenades are all affected by Explosion Mod stat
[/list]

Beyond some quality-of-life and optimization, an entire new stat was added to the game: Explosion Mod. Alongside this is a new Passive pickup that is available in the base game to increase your Explosion Mod. Shop menus are looking much cleaner and helpful, too. Beyond that was a re-configuring of Endless (and Remix) mode difficulty. Previously the difficulty curve was an amorphous thing with five tiers, it's now a much more defined 8 tier system, allowing the difficulty to get to punishing new heights. Controller players can enjoy the addition of a slight rumble as well, a small taste brought over from our burgeoning console ports.

Enjoy the Remix Update! This is not the end of Beef Cat Ultra, just another step, and we hope you follow along as the game continues to grow!

Thanks,
Kyle

notes.title: The Remix Update: Final Preview
notes.content:
Howdy Beeflandians!

We are just days away from our largest ever update, adding new stages/mode/weapons, and including tons of little tweaks. To learn more about the basics of the Remix Update, check the previous post.

I wanted to show off some of the new things you can find on Remix Island today! Let's dive in with a look at the Remix Island docks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/ec61eb0af80a4d2cf12f01dc35b0426a15052a1d.png[/img]

The Remix Island docks have a key quality of life feature: every stat upgrade shop in one convenient location! There are two NEW shops being added as well for thrill seekers. The first is the Great Reset shop. This resets every single stat shop to their default zero values. Did you buy so many damage upgrades you made the game trivial? Reset! OR! Buy in to the Remix Difficulty shop. This increases the base difficulty of the Remix Island stages, with three tiers at patch launch. This difficulty increase is steep and for folks that want a challenge and want to still endlessly buy stat increments. Difficulty too hard? The Great Reset shop will reset this one as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/86b2b33c87159ae99ff0d053527210cd51b40296.png[/img]

Shop menues got a glow-up! Alongside a font change for legibility, every shop now has a brief one line description about what is actually happening when you purchase something. This is applied to shops game-wide, not just Remix Island of course.

Back to Remix Island exclusives, let's take a look at two new weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/7363caced962e9fc06148ac779036c68536e94ce.png[/img]

Uppercut is a vertical attack that passes through all enemies in it's range. It shares a damage stat with Fisticuffs, meaning upgrading one - upgrades both. Picking up multiple Uppercuts increases the range of the attack. A new level up option on Remix Island increases the damage of fist based attacks as well. Start with Tweezer and hope for some good RNG!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/b7b022c974db4e0a85a0ca60d61bded2cc7e60ec.png[/img]

Gross Grass is a buildable weapon, placing down weeds every so often. Those weeds have a small chance every now and then to spawn friendly ticks. That spawn chance is shared with the chance that Pills have to spawn Ticks. And a new level up option in Remix Island increases the chance for both weapons to spawn ticks. Disco Debbie is looking good for this weapon.

If you caught a trend with the two new weapons shown here, there's a big emphasis on ~SYNERGIES~. Almost every new weapon, passive, or level up option can have a ripple effect on other weapons, passives, or level up options. With the randomness of Remix Island, building towards a cohesive and destructive build is inherently harder, but with a new focus on synergies your loadout can be given a whole new level of thought.

The Remix Update releases THIS WEEK (After Christmas). I'm stuffing every idea I can into the new upgrade options and then it'll be golden.

See you on Remix Island very soon,
Kyle

notes.title: The Remix Update First Look
notes.content:
Howdy Beeflandians,

I figured now would be a good time to show off some of the new content in The Remix Update. Beyond tons of little fixes and optimizations, this update has a significant infusion of ~CONTENT~. So let's dive in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/0d51256b9429dcfa2aa5180f329f316e772f7227.png[/img]

The Remix Update brings Beef Cat and Friends to Remix Island, a small island south of Stinky Coast. How do you get there? The dock in Stinky Coast of course, which will feature a new boat after beating the final boss. This is post-game content for Beeflandia's Best. Remix Island is home to four new large stages all with the new Remix Mode which for description purposes is our randomizer mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/3ed07a71344c812ee0125049c3b79adb7067cc8c.png[/img]

Navigating the new stages and mode come with a new objective - total enemy kills. Remix tasks you with defeating 5,000 enemy units before you are overwhelmed. Remix features a difficulty curve similar to Endless mode - where after periods of time, enemies have more HP and base speed. That curve is ~harder~ in Remix. Fortune favors the bold. Luckily you have access to a random pool of every piece of loot in the game, including some new items. But the loot isn't the only randomized element for you to grow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/814d08a55c87ee9c30665c0a629e83a822767ee5.png[/img]

Regardless of what character you start with, level up screens can contain the bonuses from any of the other characters, and even several completely new level up bonuses exclusive to Remix mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/bdb5e6971af9a8a36b6c11f04519c2e27a98f813.png[/img]

Fight through familiar locations, with random loot, random enemy spawns, random starting point, nearly random everything. Score victories in these stages to endlessly rack up the Remix Island clear counter - unlocking access to new shops and fun things.

---

The goal of this update is to provide endlessly repeatable content for people wanting to just sink in to some Beef Cat Ultra and find something new to challenge them. The update, content and fixes, is well under construction and will release before the end of the year! We hope you will all enjoy a fresh new take on BCU!

Thanks all,
Kyle

notes.title: What's Next for Beef Cat Ultra?
notes.content:
[h1]Beef Cat Ultra Expands Next Month![/h1]

[h2]Beef Cat Ultra: Remix Update[/h2]

Launch week is behind us, and I've been able to clean up the dust in the code. The goal has always been to grow Beef Cat Ultra over time with new ideas, content, and *stuff. I love Survivors games and I like playing my own game. So as long as I have new ideas, they will flow into the game.

The Remix Update

Let's start with a bullet point list:
[list]
[*]1 New post-game focused World with 4 New Stages
[*]1 New Mode: Remix
[*]6 New Pickups exclusively found in the new world
[*]1 New Shop for difficulty junkies
[/list]

Let's break it down!

Remix Island will become available after beating Some Big Guy! Head to the docks in Stinky Coast and set sail for a brand new mini-world featuring 4 massive sized stages using the new mode: Remix! Sharing maps with their respective Endless stages, Remix tasks you will mowing down astronomical hordes and fighting against the RNG. Everything is randomized. Pickup placement, Player Starting Point, Enemy Spawners, Jars, Chests, Mushrooms, even your level-up options. The idea is to create an endlessly replayable post-game experience for people looking for one more stage!

6 New Pickups join the loot pool on Remix Island - including Mouse Mace: Swing your mouse through the horde like never before, Uppercut: a vertically oriented melee attack, Parry Pants: drop a grenade when you successfully dodge an attack.

1 New Shop - The Anti-Shop. Pay a small fee and reset all of your permanent stat bonuses to ZERO. No refunds. An option for those that have grown in skill beyond the need for little upgrades.

The Remix Update is being prepped for a November release!

See you then!
Kyle

notes.title: Beef Cat Ultra Releases September 23rd!
notes.content:
[h1][b]September 23rd[/b][/h1]

All of us here at Team Beef Cat are absolutely stoked to be in the last legs of our journey with Beef Cat Ultra. So stoked that we've set a date - September 23rd - as the day Beeflandia is available to the public.

Next Fest was an amazing event for us to take part in and we obviously loved hearing all the great feedback people had. We are confident that BCU is a highly polished, highly entertaining title. The feedback from Next Fest led to some huge upgrades to the game as well!

Most people struggled to find the Beeflandopedia - the book of lore and stats - so it's easier to find now. A simple button press from a simple UI prompt anywhere on the World Map! Neat!

Some people thought leveling up could get a bit stale - so we added the Sticker system which adds an extra layer of RNG on top of our Paper Mario style level up screens. You still choose from 1 of 3 character specific level up options - but now they can be adorned with stickers that further grow a slew of stats each match.

We added high scores that are recorded and can be chased for every single stage. These will be bolstered by Steam Achievements for beating a developer score on every single stage. Adding another level of replayability for those more competitively inclined.

We added two local multiplayer modes - Volleyball and Deathmatch. No, there will not be local co-op of the main game of BCU but these simple, bite sized party style games will whet the whistle of folks looking to beat their friend at BCU.

And we finalized the Soundtrack album art, which will also release on September 23rd. I'll show that at the bottom of the post.

As for the other bullet points? I'll do an in depth dive on each one in the coming weeks to show off the several layers of added depth we've heaped onto the BCU experience!

Thanks everyone for following along, we will see you on September 23rd!!
Kyle

notes.title: Development Blog #3: Pickups and Meaningful Boosts
notes.content:
[h1]Development Blog #3[/h1]
[h2]Pickups and Meaningful Boosts[/h2]

Howdy again, I wanted to dive in today and rattle off some item pickups that build your character up and keep them going. I'm also gonna go into the development balance of ~how~ strong those pickups actually are - not insignificant but not easy mode. So let's go.

[h3]Assorted Pickups[/h3]

#1: Cheese 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/236a16008dc46fefd851bea08bab176264d0c906.png[/img]
Cheese is an early-game weapon pickup. It is a straight-forward dependable weapon that seeks out the closest enemy and clobbers it in dairy goodness. Additional pickups of the cheese wedge allow it to pierce more enemies. It's a low damage output, only 1 damage, but it is a guaranteed hit.

#2: Bell
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/0e93e68baff2f3a741c8475e9489263e546b2776.png[/img]
The Bell is an incredibly helpful and simple pickup. Every Bell raises your base damage by 1. In the case of a Bell and a Cheese together, you are doubling it's damage output. Very nice and good for you.

#3: Duster
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/9cc670d0bcf06d4a0a320249376f5f8aeb778935.png[/img]
The duster is another core stat builder. This one increases your chance to Dodge an enemy hit by 10%. You'll likely be taking tons of hits so even one duster pickup can mean the difference between success and being a loser.

#4: Stache
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/2a05a4d6c06b769299b6271d9c7891c47520241b.png[/img]
Stache increases your Intimidation. This is a more unique stat to Beef Cat Ultra and it effects the radius around you that enemies will be intimidated by you. By default your intimidation is 0. So enemies just run right up and smack you. But a Stache gives you 64 Intimidation, or a 64 pixel radius around you that all enemies will be affected by Intimidation. This will slow the enemy down or even make them run away from you!

#5: Watering Can
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/e026b65c74e4a592edad0134a62fedf8b6b9fc0e.png[/img]
The Watering Can plants a little flower garden in the map every 10 seconds. It looks cute and adds some nice blue flowers to your battleground. Enemies walking on you garden suffer minor damage for being jerks. 0.1 damage. Unaffected by the Bell. Which doesn't seem useful. But the Gardens also spawn coins every few seconds. Once you have several Gardens spawning coins, you'll be raking in the level-ups.

This is just 5 of the currently 30ish items in the game, a value that will grow a bunch as development continues. The idea is to have plenty of basic easy to understand items alongside some really strange ones that change the way you interact with a run, like the Water Can (do you play more sedentary to cultivate a close crop of coins?). This all boils into the larger change I worked on this week.

[h3]Make Pickups Fun[/h3]

This should feel obvious but balance and fun are a tight rope to walk. Originally, the Duster and other core stat changers adjusted a stat by 5%. Which helped a build and meant unique things would trigger here and there, but I wanted pickups to escalate the power trip faster. So I went through this week and nearly doubled every single passive pickup's output.

The issue I had is that whenever I had a choice between a new weapon or a passive pickup, I chose a weapon. The passive pickups just didn't have enough oomph. They do now. The Dropper, which used to give your weapons a 5% chance to poison an enemy now has a 10% chance. The Bracer, which reduces your weapon cooldowns, went from about 5% to around 8%. And the rate that the Watering Can planted Gardens decreased by around 2 seconds.

These changes gave a lot of life to these passive pickups that make them a lot more alluring. It speeds the game up slightly, it makes the power trip stronger, and it decreases the sometimes brutal difficulty we had as a match lasted close to the end. The chaos is more manageable if you know what you have and how to use it the best.




So there we go! A nice brief look and discussion of several pickups. This specific format of devblog will likely be used a couple more times to continue to show off items. Next week, I want to show off some different gameplay though that isn't just your standard Survivors style. Our stab at turning the Gauntlet formula into an auto-battler will be on the hot seat! Thanks for reading! And as always, if you like what you see - please wishlist, the algorithm will be happy!

Kyle

notes.title: Development Blog #2: The World Map and Controller Support
notes.content:
[h1]Development Blog #2[/h1]
[h2]The World Map and Controller Support[/h2]

Howdy howdy, last time I introduced the main character and an idea of what the "game" was like. I feel like the minute-to-minute gameplay should make sense to anyone who's played a Survivors-type game. This time, I wanted to zero in on one of the first major things we are doing to make our unique mark on the genre.

[h3]The World Map[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/1ae5a68c64ed10355502740dbbb0ed3a1561a084.png[/img]

The World of Beeflandia is progressed in a very traditional old-school Mario Bros style format. As you can see above, the HUD stays minimal. A couple key stats, a character swap panel on the left, and digestible iconography on the map. You can freely walk along the dotted lines and cross as many stages as you want. The only thing actually blocking you on your journey are Blocker Boys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/0c3de3b0b0f450673629727e2d0c6c0e8d10bef3.png[/img]

These bullies work for Some Big Guy and require a certain level of prestige to "pass" by them. That's a generous way of saying they smash into a cavalcade of pixels when you've proven yourself. That Blocker Boy is showing you need five clears. It's slightly cut off but in the first image, Beef Cat has access to six stages. What six you conquer and in which order is up to you. As long as you clear five of six, you can proceed further into Funky Forest (That's the name of World 1).

You can always peep your clears in the stats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/c2658dcb7c9469062eeea6c447f6a15b6eef0bce.png[/img]

2 Clears and 1098 Gems. The gems are an over-arching currency you collect and spend at shops on the World Map for permanent stat boosts. These are small boosts but they will add up and every coin you pick up in a stage gives you 1XP in the stage and 1 Gem in the currency pool. Replaying stages you enjoy is a perfect way to farm some gems if you just need a few more HP to beat your next stage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/39a9b9969c6cbaddb27056e77a49251409375131.png[/img]

Stages are neatly broken down into three lines to give clear instruction as fast as possible. The stage name. The Mode. And the objective. Gauntlet is one of the main modes, of which there are several (6 and counting). In Gauntlet, I'll do a post about this soon by itself, you collect keys and battle thru enemy spawners to get to an exit portal. A totally different vibe from your classic Survival. And again, we've got 6 unique modes packed in here now.

Anyways, there is a ton to tinker with and check out on the World Map, and the game will auto-save every time you return to or leave it. Now to segway into nice feature ~

[h3]Full Controller Support[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/e852629e8fe36ed80e736327fb0eacc809789035.png[/img]

Having the game completely playable with a keyboard or a controller was crucial, because it absolutely needs to be playable on Steam Deck. At the time of writing, the game is 100% ready to go for controllers and all in-game tutorials and control pop-ups dynamically reflect whether you plugged in a controller or not.

I tried to cover every possible base with controller support, so movement can be done with the analog stick or d-pad. And mapping otherwise is bog standard. It works, it works well, and I have played with a controller exclusively since getting it finished.



So yeah, there you go. Week 2. World Map and Controller Support. Beef Cat Ultra is easily the most fun I've had making a game, it embodies the mindset of "if I think of a weird idea for something, I add it in" and it has resulted in so many odd and wacky items I'll continue to show as the weeks go on. Please, follow wishlist or share. We are a super small team with barely anything as far an established audience and we want to have BCU in front of as many people as possible. If you like what you see but don't like sharing things, that's cool too - just pop in next week for the next devblog.

THANKS, kyle

notes.title: Development Blog #1: Beef Cat and Mouse Flail, Also Level Up Improvements
notes.content:
[h1]Development Blog #1[/h1]
[h2]Beef Cat and Mouse Flail, Also Level Up Improvements[/h2]

Howdy,

So this is blog #1 on Beef Cat Ultra and all the fun stuff going on in the game. I'm going to start at the most basic today and introduce the first playable character, the titular Beef Cat.

[h3]Beef Cat, Mouse Flail, and Ultra Effects[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/f96e3f0d3ee605253c3548531fb9cb75e7d68671.png[/img]

Beef Cat is your default hero, boasting no particular strengths or weaknesses. Beef Cat Ultra is in the burgeoning Survivors style of games. What this means in a nutshell is that you start every stage at Lv.1 acquiring upgrades and choosing stat boosts, adapting on the fly to the needs of your situation. Every character has three level up options divided into three categories: Weapon, Survival, and Bonus. The level up screen is paced to be a fast decision that won't bog you down.

Every character has their own starting weapon, and only they can get unique upgrades for that weapon - ultimately making it function differently than it will on the other 5 characters. Beef Cat's weapon of choice is the Mouse Flail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/9579caea6e0271b9db4e5d0cef5b35202072471d.png[/img]

This destructive mouse swung by it's tail can only hit so many enemies before breaking. Picking up additional mouse flails increases the size of the mouse. Beef Cat has unique upgrades in the level up screen to increase the number of enemies the flail can strike before breaking. There's one more ace in the sleeve of each character and their starter weapon. The also titular, Ultra effects.

Ultra effects are unique to each character and their starter weapon, unleashing chaos on the screen for a brief window of time after the trigger conditions are met. As you can see the Mouse Flail gets a little bit larger.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/801addfa3cd58e35b25c4761e6cfe5d56940c40f.png[/img]

In addition to being absolutely massive, the hit limit is removed. So when Beef Cat triggers his ultimate, the Mouse Flail sweeps the screen absolutely decimating entire hordes of enemies at once.

So yeah - each of the six playable characters has a starter weapon that they get unique upgrades for as well as a devastating Ultra skill. The goal with the different characters is to force sometimes radically different approaches to combat situations. 

[h3]Notable Work Done This Week[/h3]

I want to highlight in each blog one or two changes made in-game the week the blog is posted. A fresh piece of game that I'm proud of and want to show off. This time it's the overhaul of the level-up screen's visuals.

Let's start with the original:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/de36f90bee09bc98846ec21b577bf9f88fdf50fd.png[/img]

This was largely placeholder for most of development but I kind of got attached to the simple one word options. Play testing is good though. And our very first play tester feedback specifically mentioned wanting more info in the level-up screen. My partner also mentioned this while watching me tinker and I tend to trust her instinct. So this week, one of the goals was to finally re-vamp the screen.

This is the re-vamped level-up menu:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44934816/a75ba3adcd0485e363697f924ccc7230feb6f675.png[/img]

Not only does it pull in the three categories each character has by name, it describes the stat bonus with granular detail. I think I also still accomplished keeping a retro aesthetic despite having a much crisper and readable font. Which is good. Yay.



So yeah, this was the first little devblog! I plan on doing these weekly until launch so if you like this kinda stuff - wishlist and follow, share your thoughts. Please be kind. See you next week,

-Kyle
